rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Population ecology — growth, regulation, interactions ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Population ecology — growth** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Organisms and Environment fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  A **population** is a group of individuals of one species in one place and time. Its size (N) changes by four processes: natality (+), mortality (−), immigration (+), emigration (−). Growth follows two models — unlimited **exponential** growth or **logistic** growth limited by carrying capacity (K). Populations also interact: competition, predation, parasitism, commensalism, mutualism and amensalism.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Growth equations: exponential dN/dt = rN (J-curve, unlimited); logistic dN/dt = rN(K−N)/K (S-curve, carrying capacity K) — quote both equations and their curve shapes.  ·  Trick 2: r-strategists: small, short-lived, many offspring, unstable habitat; K-strategists: large, few offspring, stable habitat — the contrast pair.
